recommended.title: Driving through Florida during hurricane Milton is madness
recommended.description:
I drove from Jupiter to St. Petersburg before Hurricane Milton to help family prepare, then returned after the storm to check damage and move belongings. This is a first-person record of the evacuation traffic, storm preparation, an emergency tornado warning, and the recovery trip—not footage of a tornado.

This video is a personal documentary, not emergency or travel advice. Do not drive into dangerous weather. Follow evacuation orders and current guidance from local officials, the National Weather Service, and Florida emergency management.

Chapters:

2:10 Evacuation traffic heading the other way
2:28 I-275 and the Skyway approach
3:41 Boarding up and loading the cars
4:19 The day of Hurricane Milton
5:19 Emergency tornado warning
8:00 The morning after
9:55 Returning with a U-Haul
10:37 Post-storm drive into St. Petersburg
12:57 Roof and water damage
13:46 Packing belongings for the return
15:16 Final thoughts from the drive

pinnedComment.text:
A quick accuracy note: the video captures an emergency tornado warning, not footage of a tornado. I drove from Jupiter to St. Petersburg to help family prepare, sheltered back in Jupiter, then returned after Milton to check the damage and move belongings.

This is a personal record—not advice to travel during a hurricane. Follow official evacuation orders and local emergency guidance. If Milton affected you, I hope you and your family are safe.

What part of Florida's recovery do you think people overlooked?

commentReplies.text: Fair call. The current thumbnail is synthetic and oversells what the footage shows. I am replacing it with an actual frame from the trip so the packaging matches the video.
Thank you. Everyone in our group made it through. This was to help family prepare and document the aftermath, not to encourage anyone to drive during a storm.
